mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 anticipates future rate hikes, leading to negative 20-day forward returns as discounting future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following the trigger, SPX 20d returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rise is not confirmed by subsequent rate path.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 3.5% for three consecutive months predicts a labor market softening, which reduces equity risk premia and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 20d forward return is not significantly higher than the 20d forward return in the prior month's UNRATE regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising PAYEMS (labor market activity) above 158,000 in a month coincides with corporate hiring acceleration, which boosts consumer demand and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: In 20 days following the trigger, SPX 20d return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or PAYEMS does not sustain above 158,000 for the next two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in GDPC1 (real private consumption) by over 2% in a quarter suggests pent-up demand that is released in the subsequent month, generating positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >2% in a quarter
failure_condition: Within 5 days, the 20d forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or GDPC1 growth decays rapidly in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 1% in two consecutive months, it indicates supply-side weakness that elevates uncertainty and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >1% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20d forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the contraction period, or INDPRO recovers without a sustained downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST (household spending) above their prior month's levels indicate dual accommodative signals, which drive positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS up from prior month AND HOUST up from prior month
regime_hint: dual accommodative policy and consumer confidence
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the 20d forward return is not significantly higher than the 20d forward return in the prior month's regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to UNRATE below 3% combined with a 10% YoY increase in PAYEMS suggests a labor market transition that reduces wage pressure and supports positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20d forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified regime change.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) crosses above 313 for the first time in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress real returns and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns regardless of other signals.
failure_condition: The 20d forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) within 30 days of the CPI crossing, or inflation expectations revert without persistent upward pressure.
